metadata.label: Main occupation the year after higher vocational education (HVE): Key indicators for fields of education MYH. Follow-up year 2012-2025
note:
The statistics include graduates from HVE programmes that ended the year before the follow-up year. Only graduates who are registered in Sweden during the follow-up year are included..

The statistics on the proportion of graduates with employment cover all HVE graduates..

The statistics include graduates who have employment (employment or own business) both before and after their HVE programme.

The statistics on the proportion of graduates in matching jobs include those who have employment (either as an employee or self-employed).

The statistics on the proportion of graduates in more qualified job tasks include those with employment both before and after their HVE programme.

The statistics on the proportion of graduates working with workplace training employers include those with employment after their HVE programme.

The statistics on the proportion of graduates working with the same employer include those with employment both before and after their HVE programme.

The statistics on the proportion of graduates with employment within 1 or 6 months include all graduates.

The statistics on the proportion of satisfied graduates include all graduates.

The HVE programmes are classified into  fields of education areas based on the Swedish Standard Classification of Education (SUN). The detailed fields of education (SUN5) refer to the Swedish National Agency for Higher Vocational Education´s local expansion of the SUN 2020 classification. Some adjustments were made in the coding of HVE programmes in connection with the introduction of SUN 2020. Education programmess in game graphics and game design have been moved from Computers/IT to Culture, media and design (SUN 213d). Therefore, the totals for the Computers/IT and Culture, media and design education fields are not entirely comparable between 2020 and previous years.

The statistics are subject to uncertainty because not everyone responded to the survey. Therefore, a margin of error is always given. It is a range within which the true value is found with 95 percent certainty
